review_basis: Direct visual review of all packaged reference assets; no Canon authority changes.
findings: CG-A is visually well represented and internally stable.
CG-B is visually coherent but underrepresented by independent fixtures.
RDR-F01 and RDR-F07 are pixel-identical and must count as one independent CG-B example.
SC-D03 was over-classified as CG-B in V1; it is better treated as a non-diagnostic urban-depth control.
SC-D06 was over-classified as CG-B in V1; it is a useful A/B boundary leaning CG-A.
The grammar itself does not require modification based on L1.
The validation fixture map requires correction before L2.

gate_decision.condition: L2 must deliberately create additional independent CG-B coverage for VP00, VP01 and VP02.

reviews.reason: Facade plane dominates; essentially frontal/near-elevation with controlled depth. Strong CG-A positive.
Strict frontal facade special case. Confirms that retired mandatory frontality remains legal.
Facade-dominant near-elevation reading with shallow side depth.
Strong facade-dominant frontal reading with restrained perspective.
Broad frontal commercial facade. Vehicle presence is irrelevant to camera family.
Corner condition with strong side-street recession and two-plane architectural reading. Strong CG-B positive.
Pixel-identical to RDR-F01. Valid as the same CG-B example but excluded from independent coverage metrics.
Strict frontal storefront wall. Strong CG-A positive.
Street-level oblique row with strong recession, visible depth and two-point spatial reading.
Dominant industrial facade remains close to elevation despite contextual elevated structure. Moderate CG-A positive.
Flat frontal storefront block. Strong CG-A positive.
Oblique urban depth exists, but no single architectural facade/corner dominates. Useful negative/boundary control, not a clean CG-B positive.
Landscape/infrastructure composition rather than facade-dominant architectural camera. Should not calibrate CG-A/CG-B.
Dark, compressed scene with insufficient perspective cues for a robust A/B family decision.
Dominant near-frontal pharmacy plane suggests CG-A, while side-street recession introduces CG-B traits. Valuable A/B boundary fixture, not a strong CG-B positive.
